content.title: Treatment recommendations for HFpEF (excerpt)
content.summary: The Task Force notes that treatment options for HFpEF are being revised. The FDA has endorsed sacubitril/valsartan and spironolactone for some patients with LVEF below the normal range based on subgroup analyses (PARAGON-HF, PARADIGM-HF, TOPCAT) showing reductions in HF hospitalization and CV death in selected LVEF subgroups. Ongoing trials of SGLT2 inhibitors may further affect HFpEF management. In the absence of disease-modifying therapies, treatment is aimed at symptom relief (diuretics). Loop diuretics are preferred; thiazides may help with hypertension. Weight reduction and exercise are recommended where appropriate. Identifying and treating underlying risk factors and comorbidities (hypertension, CAD, amyloidosis, atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease) is important and improves outcomes.
key_medications_and_interventions: sacubitril/valsartan (endorsed by FDA for select patients with reduced LVEF within HFpEF/HFmrEF categories)
spironolactone (subgroup benefit in TOPCAT Americas cohort; EF-based analyses)
thiazide diuretics (may be useful for hypertension)
studies_cited: PARAGON-HF (sacubitril/valsartan subgroup analyses showing reduction in HF hospitalizations in LVEF <57%)
PARADIGM-HF (meta-analysis with PARAGON-HF showing reduction in CV death and HF hospitalization in those with LVEF below normal range)
TOPCAT (spironolactone subgroup in the Americas showing reduction in primary endpoint of CV death and HF hospitalization)
clinical_actions: Aim therapy at reducing congestion symptoms with diuretics
Prefer loop diuretics for congestion; consider thiazides for hypertension management
Consider weight loss and exercise to improve symptoms and exercise capacity
Identify and treat underlying aetiologies and comorbidities (see referenced sections for hypertension, CAD, amyloidosis, AF, valvular disease)

recommendations_table_summary.recommendation: Screening for, and treatment of, aetiologies and cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular comorbidities is recommended in patients with HFpEF (see relevant sections).
Diuretics are recommended in congested patients with HFpEF in order to alleviate symptoms and signs.
